stories.summary: Collapse metric groups that share a story_key, and stamp the wedge record's correlation_id
stories.description: compute_plan_rollup counts a story twice when its records are split between a correlation_id-keyed group and a story_key-keyed group. Collapse same-story_key payloads before totalling, and stamp the correlation_id on pipeline/wedge_io.py's wedge record so wedge notices stop splitting their story off into a second group.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-09-23 on ddfcab9 (scratch worktree, the real edits applied) - 0 pre-existing failures: full suite 12860 passed / 12 skipped, `ruff check .` clean.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: on-device (registry dispatch default, ~20B class). Keep the diff small and
mechanical. Two new helper functions in one file, one added kwarg in a second file.

WHY (the defect)
`compute_story_metrics` (pipeline/story_metrics.py) groups each notification record by
`correlation_id` FIRST and only falls back to `story_key`. So one story whose records carry
both shapes yields TWO payloads for one story: the records that carry a correlation_id form a
group keyed by the correlation_id, and a record that carries only a story_key forms a second
group keyed by the story key. `compute_plan_rollup` then counts that story twice -
`stories_total` is inflated, `cost_per_merged_story` is diluted, and one story's
first-pass-clean verdict is split across two payloads. The module's own docstring already
anticipates the fix: "a consumer that collapses groups sharing a story_key can only recompute
`first_pass_clean` correctly from the count".

The concrete trigger: pipeline/wedge_io.py's wedge notice passes `story_key` but never
`correlation_id`, so every wedge notice splits its story into a second group.

WHAT TO BUILD

EDIT 1 - pipeline/story_metrics.py

(a) Insert these two module-level functions immediately ABOVE `def compute_plan_rollup(`:

def _merge_payload(target: dict[str, Any], source: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Fold a second payload for the same story into the first, in place.

    Counters are summed and ``cost``/``first_pass_clean`` recomputed FROM the
    summed counters: each payload's ``cost`` already includes its own base 1,
    so summing costs would double-count the story.
    """
    for counter in (
        "dispatch_failures",
        "rework_cycles",
        "escalations",
        "disqualifying_events",
    ):
        target[counter] = (target.get(counter) or 0) + (source.get(counter) or 0)
    if target.get("correlation_id") is None and source.get("correlation_id") is not None:
        target["correlation_id"] = source["correlation_id"]
    if not target.get("merged") and source.get("merged"):
        target["merged"] = True
    if target.get("merged_ts") is None and source.get("merged_ts") is not None:
        target["merged_ts"] = source["merged_ts"]
    target["cost"] = (
        1
        + target["dispatch_failures"]
        + target["rework_cycles"]
        + target["escalations"]
    )
    target["first_pass_clean"] = (
        bool(target["merged"]) and target["disqualifying_events"] == 0
    )


def _collapse_shared_story_keys(
    stories: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Merge payloads that describe the same story into a single payload.

    ``compute_story_metrics`` groups a record by ``correlation_id`` first and
    only falls back to ``story_key``, so one story whose records carry both
    shapes yields two groups for one story - inflating ``stories_total`` and
    splitting the story's ``first_pass_clean`` across two payloads.

    Payloads with no ``story_key`` are returned untouched: two correlation_id
    groups are two stories, and the keyless bucket is not a story at all.
    Merged payloads are copies, so the inputs are never mutated.
    """
    collapsed: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    position_by_key: dict[str, int] = {}
    for story in stories:
        story_key = story.get("story_key")
        if story_key is None:
            collapsed.append(dict(story))
            continue
        position = position_by_key.get(str(story_key))
        if position is None:
            position_by_key[str(story_key)] = len(collapsed)
            collapsed.append(dict(story))
            continue
        _merge_payload(collapsed[position], story)
    return collapsed

(b) In `compute_plan_rollup`, make the collapse the FIRST statement of the body and add one
    sentence to the docstring, so the body starts:

    stories = _collapse_shared_story_keys(stories)
    stories = [
        story
        for story in stories
        if story.get("story_key") is not None or story.get("correlation_id") is not None
    ]
    stories_total = len(stories)

    Docstring sentence to add (after the existing first paragraph):
    "Payloads are first collapsed per ``story_key`` (``_collapse_shared_story_keys``), so a
    story the producer split across a correlation_id group and a story_key group counts once."

In the wedge emit, add the conditional correlation_id spread as the LAST kwarg (this is the

stories.summary: Count a dispatch watchdog kill as a rework cycle
stories.description: A watchdog kill is checkpointed and re-dispatched - a genuine rework cycle - but the kill path emits no record, so rework_cycles, cost and cost_per_merged_story under-count every story the watchdog had to kill. Emit a dispatch_watchdog_timeout record from the single block both kill routes converge on, and count that event as rework (cost) but never as a first-pass disqualifier.

Preflight: impact run 2026-09-23 on ddfcab9 (scratch worktree, the real edits applied) - 0 pre-existing failures: full suite 12860 passed / 12 skipped, `ruff check .` clean. TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (PIPELINE_BACKEND_DISPATCH is unset; this story edits

tier - so it must not run on-device). Pin: backend "ollama", model "glm-5.3-flash:cloud".

DEPENDS ON RLF-1 ("Collapse metric groups that share a story_key..."): both stories edit
pipeline/story_metrics.py. Do not start until RLF-1 has merged, and re-read
`_REWORK_EVENTS` after rebasing - RLF-1 leaves it untouched, but rebase before editing.

WHY (the defect)
When the dispatch watchdog kills a story, the story is checkpointed and re-dispatched - a
genuine rework cycle. But the kill path emits no notification record at all, so
`compute_story_metrics` never counts it: `rework_cycles` and `cost` are under-reported for
every story the watchdog had to kill, and `cost_per_merged_story` in the plan report is
wrong-low. There is no record an operator can read either - the kill is only visible in the
story's own transcript.

WHAT TO BUILD (2 edits, 2 files, 0 new functions)

EDIT 1 - pipeline/story_metrics.py: add the new event name to `_REWORK_EVENTS`, so:

_REWORK_EVENTS = frozenset(
    {
        "tests_failed",
        "merge_ci_rework",
        "merge_gate_retry",
        "merge_retry",
        "dispatch_watchdog_timeout",
    }
)

Rationale (state this in the commit body): a watchdog kill + re-dispatch IS a rework cycle, so
it counts toward `rework_cycles`/`cost` - but it is NOT a first-pass disqualifier, because a
kill is usually environment/activity-caused rather than a wrong first attempt. That is exactly
what the standing invariant comment above `_FIRST_PASS_DISQUALIFYING_EVENTS` says about rework
events. DO NOT EDIT that comment block or that set:
tests/unit/test_plan_rollup_uncorrelated.py::test_disqualifying_events_definition_carries_a_rework_comment
reads the comment lines directly above the definition and asserts they mention "rework" and
"first"/"clean", and forbid the phrases "for now", "rpt-1" and "this task".

EDIT 2 - pipeline/story_status.py: insert ONE `_notify_user` call inside the watchdog kill
branch, immediately AFTER the `_terminate_and_checkpoint(...)` call and BEFORE the
`_rebrief_step_cap_struggle(...)` call that follows it, so the block reads:

                    story["watchdog_streak"] = story.get("watchdog_streak", 0) + 1
                    _terminate_and_checkpoint(
                        manifest,

                        plan_name,

                        pid=pid,
                        step="dispatch_watchdog_timeout",
                        summary=watchdog_summary,
                    )

                        plan_name,
                        f"{story_key} killed by the dispatch watchdog; the "
                        f"re-dispatch counts as a rework cycle.",
                        story_key=story_key,
                        severity="warning",
                        event="dispatch_watchdog_timeout",
                        **({"correlation_id": story["correlation_id"]} if story.get("correlation_id") else {}),
                    )
                    _rebrief_step_cap_struggle(  # noqa: F821

Why ONE insertion is enough: both kill routes (stale activity, and the wall-clock backstop for

branch below it.

stories.summary: Emit brief_patched from the step-cap rebrief and attribute its unsatisfiable notice
stories.description: pipeline/dispatch_attempt.py's _rebrief_step_cap_struggle rewrites a dispatched story's agent_instructions without emitting brief_patched, so compute_story_metrics reports the story clean while local_success's classifier reports it not-clean. Emit the record only when the brief actually changed, and stamp the unsatisfiable notice with story_key.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-09-23 on ddfcab9 (scratch worktree, the real edits applied, including the four authorized edits below) - 0 failures left after them: full suite 12860 passed / 12 skipped, `ruff check .` clean. The four authorized edits are REQUIRED: without them, tests/unit/test_acceptance_rebrief_unsatisfiable_wire.py fails 2 tests, because its recorder rejects the new keyword and its "no notification" assertions did not distinguish the new record from the unsatisfiable one.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: on-device (registry dispatch default, ~20B class). ONE production file,
ONE new helper-free edit block, 0 new functions.

WHY (the defect)
`_rebrief_step_cap_struggle` (pipeline/dispatch_attempt.py) REWRITES a dispatched story's
`agent_instructions` - it folds in the diagnosis and the measured facts. That is exactly the
event `brief_patched` exists for (the `patch_story` MCP tool emits it for the same change), but
this path emits nothing. The consequence is two reports disagreeing about the same story:
`pipeline/local_success.py`'s classifier sees the rewritten brief (its header marker) and
records the story as NOT a clean first pass, while `compute_story_metrics` sees no
disqualifying event and reports it as clean. One report, two verdicts.
Second, smaller defect in the same function: its unsatisfiable notice is emitted without
`story_key`, so the record lands in the `<uncorrelated>` bucket and cannot be attributed.

WHAT TO BUILD

EDIT 1 - pipeline/dispatch_attempt.py, in `_rebrief_step_cap_struggle`

(a) Capture the brief as it was on entry, right after the evidence collection:

    facts = collect_attempt_facts(worktree, story)
    evidence = collect_failure_evidence(worktree, story, facts=facts)
    previous_instructions = story.get("agent_instructions", "")

(b) At the very end of the function, after the facts compose, add the emit. The final lines of
    the function must become exactly:

    story["agent_instructions"] = compose_attempt_facts(
        story.get("agent_instructions", ""), facts)
    if story["agent_instructions"] != previous_instructions:
        try:
            _notify_user(
                plan_name,
                f"{story_key} brief rewritten after a step-cap struggle; the "
                f"resume carries the folded diagnosis.",
                story_key=story_key,
                event="brief_patched",
                **({"correlation_id": story["correlation_id"]} if story.get("correlation_id") else {}),
            )
        except Exception:
            logging.getLogger("pipeline").debug(
                "brief_patched notify failed during step-cap rebrief", exc_info=True)

    Why this shape:
    - The `!= previous_instructions` guard is the same contract the `patch_story` MCP tool
      uses (pipeline/service.py): emit only when the text ACTUALLY changed. A no-op diagnosis
      with no facts leaves the brief byte-identical, and that must not be reported as a patch.
    - Emit only after BOTH composes have run - the change is only real once
      `compose_attempt_facts` has had its turn.
    - The try/except mirrors the unsatisfiable notice above it in the same function: this
      routine is fail-open by construction and must never raise or block a retry.
    - `logging` is already imported in this module; do not add imports.
    - `plan_name`/`story_key` are already threaded in by every call site (the existing
      unsatisfiable notice passes `plan_name` unguarded already) - do not add defaults or

Preflight: impact run 2026-09-23 on ddfcab9 (scratch worktree, this story's exact CSS applied plus the authorized re-pin below) - 0 pre-existing failures: full suite 12860 passed / 12 skipped, `ruff check .` clean. WHY (the defect)
The dashboard notification toast does not handle long text. The plan-completion notification's
message is a multi-line, "
"-joined plan summary (pipeline/plan_summary.py's
`format_plan_summary`) and it renders badly in the 320px toast: the newlines collapse into one
run-on line, a long URL overflows the box (no `overflow-wrap`, and `.toast-msg` has no
`min-width: 0`, so a flex item's automatic minimum size refuses to shrink below its longest
token), the key column wraps into a tall stack ("reporting-/attribution-/fix"), and
`align-items: center` vertically centres the short key against a tall multi-line message.

WHAT TO BUILD - static/style.css, three adjacent rules in the `/* Toast stack styles */` block
Replace exactly these three lines:

.toast-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-2); }
.toast-key { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--fs-xs); color: var(--stripe, var(--text-muted)); }
.toast-msg { flex: 1; }

with exactly these three lines:

.toast-row { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--sp-2); }
.toast-key { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--fs-xs); color: var(--stripe, var(--text-muted)); flex-shrink: 0; white-space: nowrap; }
.toast-msg { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; white-space: pre-line; max-height: 40vh; overflow-y: auto; }

Each addition has a reason, and each is required:
- `align-items: flex-start` - keep the key at the top of a multi-line message instead of
  centring it.
- `.toast-key`'s `flex-shrink: 0; white-space: nowrap` - the key is a short identifier and
  must not be wrapped or squeezed by a long message.
- `.toast-msg`'s `min-width: 0` - the actual overflow fix: a flex item's default
  `min-width: auto` prevents shrinking below its longest unbreakable token.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` - break a long URL instead of letting it overflow the toast.
- `white-space: pre-line` - honour the summary's newlines (which `innerHTML` inserts as real
  text) while still collapsing runs of spaces.
- `max-height: 40vh; overflow-y: auto` - a long summary must not run off the screen; it scrolls
  within the toast instead.
